historical_references.reference: Shareeq Al-Mamoon, the Abbasid caliph known for his tolerant attitude towards various religious groups, including Christians and Jews, built a canal known as Shareeq Al-Hadid (Iron Bridge) or Shareeq Al-Mamoon to connect the Tigris and Euphrates rivers in Baghdad, Iraq, around 836 AD.

Shareeq Al-Mousa, a Yemeni scholar, is considered one of the earliest authorities on Hadith literature and was a prominent figure in the formation of the Islamic legal and scholarly tradition. He is also known as Al-Kulayni, and his collection of Hadith, Al-Kafi, is one of the most important sources of Shia Islamic law. Shareeq Al-Mousa lived during the late 9th and early 10th centuries AD (around 864-941 AD).
